scenes.heading: What is Data Engineering?
scenes.subheading: Building the pipelines that move and shape data
scenes.narration: Data engineering is the discipline of designing and building the systems that collect, store, and prepare data so that others can use it reliably.

scenes.heading: What data engineers build
bullets: Pipelines that move data from sources into storage
Transformations that clean and reshape raw data
Storage systems like warehouses and lakes
Infrastructure that makes data trustworthy and available
scenes.narration: Engineers build pipelines because raw data rarely arrives where analysts need it. They write transformations because source data is messy and must be cleaned before use. They choose storage systems so that data can be queried efficiently at scale. And they maintain the infrastructure so that the whole flow stays reliable and available.

scenes.heading: The path data travels
scenes.narration: Data begins in operational sources such as apps and databases, and engineers ingest it into a central store. From there it is transformed into clean, modeled tables. Finally it is served to analysts, dashboards, and machine learning systems that turn it into value.

scenes.heading: Data engineering vs data analysis
scenes.narration: Data engineering is concerned with building the plumbing that delivers clean, dependable data. Data analysis, by contrast, is concerned with drawing meaning from that data once it arrives. The two roles depend on each other, but the engineer builds the foundation the analyst stands on.

scenes.text: Data engineering builds the reliable foundation that lets everyone else turn raw data into insight and action.
scenes.narration: In short, data engineering is the foundation of every data-driven organization, quietly enabling analytics, reporting, and machine learning.
